model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth, AT1 and preference distributions charged in the flow

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: terminal nominal growth for a mature Chinese state bank (China nominal GDP ~4-5% less continued NIM drift and policy-directed lending), bracketed by revenue 5yr CAGR 1.5% and BVPS 5yr CAGR 5.6%; the DCF's base revenue path runs 4.0% -> 3.0%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Ordinary equity 3yr/5yr CAGR 10.5%/9.3% vs revenue 1.1%/1.5% and EPS -1.8%/+1.8% (>30% apart). Equity growth is retained earnings plus the RMB120bn FY2025 placement (shares 74,263m -> 88,364m), not operating growth; per-share book compounds at 4-6%. Revenue stalled because NIM fell from 1.58% (FY2019) to 1.20% (FY2025) while the balance sheet grew ~8%/yr. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: a bank's reported FCF (OCF - capex) is deposit-flow noise (-99.5bn FY2024, +89.2bn FY2025, +336.6bn FY2022). The relevant series is net profit attributable to ordinary shareholders: 86,122 (FY2024) -> 88,920 (FY2025), +3.2%; H1 2026 ordinary profit 46,189 vs 44,331, +4.2%, but EPS 0.52 vs 0.59 (-11.9%) on the enlarged share base. Revenue FY2020 246,724 / FY2022 257,346 -> FY2025 265,600; EPS 0.99 / 1.14 -> 1.08; attributable equity 866,607 / 1,022,024 -> 1,269,232; ordinary equity (less perpetual/preference instruments) 733,315 / 847,234 -> 1,142,782; BVPS 9.87 / 11.41 -> 12.93 RMB; net profit 78,274 / 92,102 -> 95,622.

scenario_narratives.base: BoCom as a steady-state G-SIB: net operating income grows 4% fading to 3%, pre-tax margin holds 39.5%, CET1 is held at 11.0% so retention absorbs 24% of revenue in FY2027 falling to 13% by FY2036 as RWA growth slows to 3%. FCFE ramps from ~RMB27bn (FY2027) to ~RMB78bn (FY2036); the >30% dividend is only fully covered from about FY2029-30, so CET1 drifts lower in the interim. Terminal ROE ~7.3%, implied terminal P/B ~0.64x.
scenario_narratives.bull: NIM troughs at 1.2% and recovers toward 1.35% as deposit repricing outlasts asset repricing; fee income resumes growth; credit cost falls to ~0.6% as property/LGFV resolution completes. Pre-tax margin reaches 41.5%; FCFE covers the dividend from FY2028. Terminal ROE ~8%.
scenario_narratives.bear: NIM resumes compression toward 1.05%, retail credit stress (credit-card NPL 2.68%) lifts credit cost toward 0.95%, and the policy mandate keeps RWA growing 7% while revenue stalls. FCFE collapses to RMB6-10bn a year against a RMB31bn dividend, forcing a payout cut or a second discounted state placement (the 2025 one was at 0.66x book). Terminal ROE ~6%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth the equity cash flow it can distribute after funding the capital its regulator and its own growth require, discounted at the cost of equity. BoCom's reported profit (~RMB95bn) overstates distributable earnings because RWA growth of 6-7% at an 11% CET1 target absorbs ~RMB70bn a year; the dividend currently exceeds FCFE and is funded by capital-ratio drift. The valuation credits only the FCFE, lets it ramp as balance-sheet growth converges on nominal GDP, and charges every AT1 coupon and preference dividend in the flow. The 2025 placement at 0.66x book is the template for how the state resolves a capital shortfall here: dilution, not a dividend cut, so the per-share value is what matters.
key_risks_to_valuation: A second discounted state placement (the 2025 one added 19% to the share count at 0.66x book) if RWA growth keeps outrunning FCFE; the flat share count ignores it.
NIM: at 1.20-1.23% BoCom has the lowest margin of the big six; each 10bp is ~RMB14bn of NII (~5% of revenue) on a RMB14tn interest-earning balance sheet.
Retail credit quality: credit-card NPL 2.68%, personal-loan NPL 1.58% and rising; provision coverage 203.8% is the buffer.
Property (5.65% of loans at 4.20% NPL) and local-government-debt exposures still being worked out.
State-directed lending under the 'Five Priorities' allocates credit for policy, not return; ROE has fallen from 10.8% (FY2021) to 8.1% (H1 2026).
CNY/HKD translation for the H-share holder; the A/H premium (~16%) can widen or close independently of fundamentals.
Cost of equity: the 10Y CGB (~1.8%) was assumed, not fetched; +/-1pt on CoE moves the base value ~15-20%.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (3328.HK, HKD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 6.35-8.70. CNYHKD=X and 601328.SS from the same source, same day.
data_sources.financials: research/3328.HK/Reports/3328.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2018-FY2025 annual, H1 FY2023-FY2026 interim) built from the H-share annual reports and interim reports in research/3328.HK/Extracted/; H1 2026 interim report (balance sheet p.5180-5200 of the text, RWA and capital ratios p.300-321, income statement p.1700-1706, note 32 other equity instruments); FY2025 annual report (five-year highlights p.375-410, RWA p.421, outlook p.3463-3560, ordinary-shareholder profit p.12039).
data_sources.qualitative: research/3328.HK/Reports/3328.HK_Analysis.json (guidance, risks, bull/bear cases) and the FY2025 outlook section; management guides qualitatively only (NIM 'overall stability', payout >30%, 'Five Priorities' loan-mix expansion, no numeric targets).

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E net operating income, RMB m: H1 2026 actual 142,540 (interim p.5, +6.77% YoY; NII 92,592 +8.6%, fees 20,473 flat, other income flat) + H2 2026E 136,460 (H2 2025 actual 132,102 x 1.033; H2 is seasonally the weaker half). FY2025 actual 265,600, so FY2026E is +5.0%. Revenue = the Group's 'net operating income' line (NII + net fee and commission income + other operating income).
inputs.share_count_basis: 88,363,784,223 A + H ordinary shares at 30 June 2026 (interim p.3 and balance sheet share capital RMB88,364m at RMB1 par), after the RMB120bn A-share placement to the Ministry of Finance, China National Tobacco and China Shuangwei completed mid-2025 (74,263m -> 88,364m, +19%). One class, same economic rights, so the per-share value applies to the H share. Held FLAT: no SBC, no buyback programme; the 450m domestic preference shares (RMB45bn) convert only on a CET1 trigger (5.125%) and are not modelled; a further state recapitalisation at a discount to book is the dilution the flat count ignores (see notes).
inputs.debt_cash_note: Bank: deposits (RMB9.92tn), certificates of deposit (RMB1.36tn), debt securities issued (RMB713bn, incl. TLAC non-capital bonds) and interbank funding are operating funding; cash and central-bank balances are liquidity, not surplus. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route; nothing is bridged after the flows. The CSV's TotalDebt (debt securities issued, 692,085 at FY2025) is bank balance-sheet leverage and is deliberately not used.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E FCFE = net profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders ~94.9bn (PBT ~111.6bn at a 40.0% pre-tax margin: H1 actual 53,637 + H2E ~58,000; less income tax ~9%, NCI ~1.3% and AT1/preference distributions ~4.7% = 15.0%) LESS equity retained to hold CET1 at 11.0% on 6.5% RWA growth (0.065 x 0.11 x 9,958,343 = 71.2bn). Reported OCF - capex (FY2025: 132,441 - 43,197 = 89,244; FY2024: -99,523) is deposit/interbank flow noise and is not used. FY2026E ordinary dividend (~31bn at a 31% payout: interim 14,845 paid, final ~16bn) EXCEEDS FCFE by ~7bn, which is why CET1 drifted 11.43% -> 11.25% in H1 2026 despite the placement.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: no share-based payment scheme in the FY2018-FY2025 annual reports (StockBasedComp blank/0 and ShareRepurchases 0 in every CSV period; EquityAwardTaxes 0); basic = diluted EPS (RMB1.08 FY2025). House and street bases coincide; band_position is degenerate.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model; the Bank reports in RMB) to HKD (H-share quote): CNYHKD=X 1.1748 at 2026-10-22T08:26Z, Yahoo Finance chart API (HKD per CNY, so HKD value = CNY value x 1.1748). Direction check: 0998.HK/0939.HK/1658.HK use the same 1.17 convention; 1 CNY ~ 1.17 HKD is the right way round (CNY is the stronger unit). The Shanghai A share (601328.SS) closed at CNY 8.21 = HKD 9.64 on the same day, a ~16% A/H premium that is normal for Chinese banks, so the dual listing is not a parity check. Per-share values are per ordinary share and apply equally to A and H shares. Known project bug: sanity_check.py may apply fx in the wrong direction when printing multiples; the DCF JSON values are correct.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.ordinary_equity_note: Equity attributable to shareholders of the parent 1,292,792 LESS other equity instruments 124,952 (preference shares 44,952 + perpetual bonds 80,000; interim balance sheet, note 32) = ordinary equity RMB1,167,840m at 30 June 2026, BVPS RMB13.22 = HKD15.53; FY2025 reported NAPS RMB12.93. The H share at HKD8.32 trades at 0.54x book. CET1 capital 11.25% x RWA 10,334,314 = 1,162,610, within 0.5% of ordinary equity, so the 11.0% CET1 target maps almost 1:1 onto ordinary book.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single CNY cost of equity 9.75% in every scenario (risk is charged once, through the scenario weights, not by moving the discount rate). Built in the flows' own currency: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% (ASSUMPTION, not fetched; the PBOC easing cycle has had the 10Y CGB in the 1.6-2.0% range since 2025) + beta ~1.05 x China ERP ~6.5% = ~8.6%, plus ~1.15pt for risks a CSI-300 ERP does not price for an H-share holder in a state bank: state-directed lending under the 'Five Priorities' (technology >16%, green and inclusive >10% each of loans), majority MOF/state control with the payout set by the state and no buyback lever, capital-account/RMB translation risk for the HKD holder. Set 0.25pt ABOVE the 9.5% used for CCB (0939.HK) and PSBC (1658.HK) because BoCom is the smallest and lowest-return of the big six (ROE 8.09% annualised H1 2026 vs 9-10% for the Big Four, NIM 1.23% the lowest in the group) and needed the largest relative recapitalisation (19% dilution), and 0.75pt BELOW CITIC (0998.HK) 10.5% because BoCom is a G-SIB (bucket 1 since Nov 2023) with CET1 11.25% against an 8.5% minimum, MOF-backed. Hurdle for entry price is the house 15%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities RMB6.3bn are immaterial against RMB15.5tn of assets and are left inside operating expenses; no lease charge path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests (RMB11.1bn of equity; RMB732m of H1 2026 profit, ~1.3% of PBT) are charged inside cash_tax_rate_path so that EBIT x (1 - rate) = profit to ordinary shareholders of the parent.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for Chinese banks (0939.HK CCB, 1658.HK PSBC, 0998.HK CITIC, 2016.HK CZB). First valuation of this ticker, no MEMORY.md entry. Not an owner-FCF DCF: deposits are operating funding, OCF swings from -222bn (H1 2024) to +368bn (FY2022) and is meaningless, net debt is zero by construction and no debt or cash is bridged. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = net operating income; ebitda_margin = pre-tax profit margin AFTER credit impairment (the real cost of a bank; FY2023 38.6%, FY2024 39.8%, FY2025 39.1%, H1 2026 37.6%); sbc, D&A, leases and working capital all zero; cash_tax_rate = income tax (~9%, low because of tax-exempt government-bond interest; FY2025 ~7%, H1 2026 9.4%) + NCI (~1.3%) + AT1 perpetual-bond interest and preference dividends (~4.7%: RMB80bn perps at ~2.1-4.2% plus RMB45bn prefs at 4.07% = ~5.2bn) = 15.0-15.5% of PBT, so EBIT x (1 - rate) = net profit to ORDINARY shareholders (FY2025 actual 88,920 on PBT 103,763 = 14.3%); capex = equity retained to hold CET1 at 11.0% on RWA growth (g_RWA x 11.0% x prior-year RWA, as % of revenue), so FCF = FCFE = distributable earnings. Terminal growth applies to FCFE at the cost of equity; terminal_cap_multiple 18x FCFE is above the Gordon multiple in every scenario (14.8x base at 9.75%-3.0%) and does not bind. KEY FINDINGS: (1) The RMB120bn placement lifted CET1 from 10.24% to 11.43%, but RWA grew 3.8% in H1 2026 alone and the dividend (~31bn/yr, >30% payout policy, 14th consecutive year) exceeds FY2026E FCFE (~24bn), so CET1 is already drifting back down (11.25% at June 2026). The valuation credits only the FCFE, which ramps as RWA growth slows from ~6.5% to ~3%; the dividend is funded by capital-ratio drift until about FY2029-30 in the base case. (2) Dilution: the placement at ~RMB8.51/share (120,000 / 14,101m shares) was at 0.66x FY2024 book, so it transferred value from existing holders; EPS fell 1.16 -> 1.08 despite +2.2% profit. A second placement is the main bear-case risk the flat share count ignores. (3) NIM 1.20% (FY2025) is the lowest among the big six; H1 2026 +2bp YoY to 1.23% is the first stabilisation after five years of compression from 1.58% (FY2019). Management guides only to 'maintain overall stability' of NIM, payout >30%, no numeric targets. QUALITATIVE: 3328.HK_Analysis.json (read) confirms the drivers without moving any path: property loans 5.65% of book at 4.20% NPL (improving from 4.85%), retail NPL rising (credit card 2.68%, personal 1.58%), provision coverage 203.8% off the 208.4% peak, ROE 10.76% (FY2021) -> 8.38% (FY2025) -> 8.09% (H1 2026 annualised). Valuation date is 9.7 months into FY2026, so FY2026E is fy0 (not discounted) and the first discounted flow is FY2027; the FY2025 final dividend (paid July 2026) and the FY2026 interim (14,845m, paid Dec 2026/Jan 2027) are paid out of fy0 and are not double-counted.

bear.growth_rationale: NIM resumes compression (further LPR cuts, mortgage repricing) toward ~1.05%, offsetting balance-sheet growth; revenue flat for three years, then 2%.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit cost rises toward 0.95% on retail (credit-card NPL 2.68%, personal 1.58%) and residual property/LGFV losses; provision coverage used as a buffer then rebuilt. Margin back to the FY2020 level of ~35-36%.
bear.capex_rationale: Policy-directed balance-sheet growth continues while revenue stalls: RWA growth 7.0%, 6.5, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0 at CET1 11.0% (retention RMB81.7bn FY2027 -> 54.3bn FY2036), over the bear revenue path. FY2027 FCFE is ~RMB6bn against a ~31bn dividend, i.e. the dividend is cut or a second dilutive state placement follows.
bear.tax_rationale: Fixed AT1 coupons and NCI are a larger share of a smaller PBT; 16.0%.
bear.narrative: NIM keeps falling, credit cost rises, RWA growth outpaces earnings; FCFE is a fraction of the dividend and capital must be rebuilt by cutting the payout or diluting again. Terminal ROE ~6%.

base.growth_rationale: Net operating income +4.0% for two years, 3.5% for two, then 3.0%: NIM stabilising at ~1.2% (H1 2026 +2bp YoY after -38bp over five years), balance sheet growing ~6-7% slowing to ~3%, fee income flat (H1 2026 +0.1%), other income flat. Below RWA growth in the early years, so NI/RWA keeps drifting down and terminal ROE settles ~7.3%.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin after credit impairment held at 39.5%: FY2023 38.6%, FY2024 39.8%, FY2025 39.1%, FY2026E ~40.0% (H1 37.6% with cost-to-income down 2.5pt to 27.5% and credit impairment +5.3%; H2 is seasonally stronger on PBT because the preference dividend and year-end provisioning fall in H2 but revenue timing favours H2 PBT). Base assumes credit cost ~0.75% of loans, cost-to-income ~28-29%, no NIM recovery.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold CET1 at 11.0% on RWA growth of 6.0%, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 4.0, 3.5, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0 from FY2026E RWA RMB10,605bn (FY2025 9,958bn; H1 2026 10,334bn, +3.8% in six months). RWA grew 6.0% FY2023, 6.4% FY2024, 5.7% FY2025. Retention / revenue: 0.06 x 0.11 x 10,605,000 / 290,160 = 24.1% in FY2027, falling to 13.3% as RWA growth converges on terminal growth. Terminal-year (FY2036) RWA ~15,995bn, ordinary equity ~RMB1,760bn, terminal ROE ~7.3%. CET1 11.0% is 2.5pt above the 8.5% G-SIB bucket-1 minimum (4.5% + 2.5% conservation + 1.0% G-SIB surcharge, plus any D-SIB/TLAC overlay) and slightly below the 11.25% at June 2026, consistent with management's silence on a further raise.
base.tax_rationale: Income tax ~9.5% (FY2025 ~7%, H1 2026 9.4%; low because of tax-exempt government-bond and fund-distribution income) + NCI ~1.3% + AT1 perpetual-bond interest and preference dividends ~4.7% = 15.5% of PBT, held flat (FY2025 actual 14.3%). Coupons on RMB80bn perpetuals (RMB41.5bn refinanced in H1 2026 at ~2%) and RMB45bn preference shares (4.07%) are fixed in RMB, so the percentage falls slightly as PBT grows; ignored (conservative).
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 9.75% - 3.0% = 14.8x; the 18x cap does not bind in any scenario. It binds only in the sensitivity grid's lowest cost-of-equity row, which is the cap doing its job: a bank earning ~7% on equity is not worth 20x+ its distributable earnings. Implied terminal P/B ~0.64x on terminal ROE ~7.3%, consistent with (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) = (7.3 - 3.0)/(9.75 - 3.0).
base.narrative: Steady-state state bank: NIM holds ~1.2%, credit cost ~0.75%, RWA growth decelerates from 6.5% to 3%, CET1 held at 11.0%, and the >30% dividend becomes fully covered by FCFE around FY2029-30. No second recapitalisation.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM recovers modestly (deposit repricing tailwind outlasts LPR cuts, 1.23% -> ~1.35%), fee income returns to low-single-digit growth as wealth-management and custody scale, balance sheet keeps growing ~6%.
bull.margin_rationale: Credit cost eases toward 0.6% as the property and LGFV work-out completes (property NPL already 4.85% -> 4.20%), cost-to-income holds the H1 2026 27.5%; margin reaches the FY2021 level of ~41.5%.
bull.capex_rationale: Same RWA path and 11.0% CET1 target as base (retention RMB70.0bn FY2027 falling to 51.2bn FY2036) over the higher bull revenue path.
bull.tax_rationale: AT1 coupons fixed in RMB shrink as a share of a larger PBT; 15.0%.
bull.narrative: NIM troughs and recovers, credit cost normalises, fee growth returns; terminal ROE ~8%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (house default for Chinese state banks, same as CCB/0939.HK and PSBC/1658.HK, below CITIC/0998.HK's 35%): BoCom is a G-SIB with MOF backing and CET1 11.25% just rebuilt by the placement, so solvency is not the bear case; the bear case is the lowest NIM in the group compressing further, rising retail credit cost, and the dividend being funded by capital drift until another dilutive raise. Bull 20%: NIM has only just stopped falling, fee income is flat, and the policy-lending mandate caps upside. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
